summary: In this story, a girls' volleyball team that struggles with communication on the court learns to call out plays and support each other, and plays their most coordinated match yet at the school tournament.
introduce: Act out a short mime, such as checking your watch and tapping your foot, and ask students how you feel and how they know. Explain that in “The Volleyball Tournament” they will use clues in the same way to work out what the writer does not say directly.

keyTerms.def: the particular spot or role a player has on a team
a person who plays on the same team as you
something done wrong, often by accident

challengeTerms.def: to work together smoothly so that actions fit well with each other
to crash into something or someone with force
a careful plan used to reach a goal

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that talking to your teammates matters more than individual skill? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how the team's new habits helped them improve.
struggling: Pre-teach position, teammate, and mistake with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses coordinate, collide, and strategy to make an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
